quadrants.goldilocks: Goldilocks (growth above trend, inflation below target)
quadrants.overheating: Overheating / Reflation (growth above trend, inflation above target)
quadrants.stagflation: Stagflation (growth below trend, inflation above target)
quadrants.slowdown: Disinflationary slowdown (growth below trend, inflation below target)

indicators.label: Atlanta Fed GDPNow (current qtr, % saar)
indicators.note: Nowcast of current-quarter real GDP; gap = value - trend.

indicators.label: Real GDP, last quarter (% saar)
indicators.note: Latest BEA print; gap = value - trend.

indicators.label: Chicago Fed National Activity Index, 3m avg
indicators.note: CFNAI = 0 means trend growth; heuristic: 1 index pt ~ 1.5pp of growth.

indicators.label: Nonfarm payrolls, 3m avg change (k)
indicators.note: Gap vs ~80k/month breakeven (low immigration era); 60k ~ 1pp. Heuristic.

indicators.label: Unemployment rate, 6m change in 3m avg (pp)
indicators.note: Okun's law: +0.5pp/yr unemployment ~ -1pp growth, so 6m change x -4.

indicators.label: Industrial production, 6m annualized (%)
indicators.note: IP trend ~1%/yr and ~2x as volatile as GDP, so scaled by 0.5.

indicators.label: Initial claims, 4wk avg vs 52wk avg (%)
indicators.note: Claims 10% above their 1y average ~ -1pp growth. Heuristic.

indicators.label: Real retail sales, 3m annualized (%)
indicators.note: Nominal retail sales deflated by headline CPI; volatile, scaled by 0.5.

indicators.label: Chicago Fed NFCI (financial conditions)
indicators.note: Leading: negative NFCI = looser than average = supports growth.

indicators.label: Core PCE, y/y (%)
indicators.note: The Fed's target measure; gap = value - 2%.

indicators.label: Core CPI, 3m annualized (%)
indicators.note: CPI runs ~0.4pp above PCE, so gap = value - 2.4%.

indicators.label: Headline CPI, 6m annualized (%)
indicators.note: Includes energy (volatile, so 6m window and half weight); gap = value - 2.4%.

indicators.label: 10y breakeven inflation (%)
indicators.note: Market-implied CPI inflation; ~0.3pp CPI/PCE + risk premium wedge.

indicators.label: UMich 1y inflation expectations (%)
indicators.note: Survey runs ~1pp above realized PCE on average; half weight on the gap.

model.caveat: History uses current-vintage FRED data with approximate publication lags, not true real-time vintages.

views.name: BlackRock Investment Institute
views.title: Inflation: beyond the Mideast energy shock (Weekly commentary)
views.summary: Energy shock's US inflation boost (+1.5pp in Sept) has likely peaked and should reverse to -0.8pp drag by end-2027 as crude/gasoline fall. US growth holds steady while tight labor keeps core services sticky; thinks market pricing of further Fed hikes is overdone.
key_points: Mideast energy shock reverses from +1.5pp boost to -0.8pp drag by YE-2027
Headline inflation cooling in 2027; core services remain sticky
US economic growth holds relatively steady; AI buildout transition risks watched
Market pricing of further Fed hikes looks excessive; favors short/medium Treasuries
quotes: We think the energy shock's impact on U.S. inflation has peaked. Brent crude oil, gasoline and diesel prices have all fallen sharply this month, which should help ease headline inflation and core inflation through lower prices for transportation services.
We see headline inflation cooling in 2027, even as markets price in more Fed hikes than we expect.
views.scoring_rationale: Qualitative growth ('holds relatively steady', watching AI buildout-to-adoption transition from Nov 9/16 Forum) -> +0.3 with sd 0.8. Headline inflation cooling from ~3% while services stay sticky -> +0.6 (sd 0.65).

views.name: Goldman Sachs Research
views.title: US Economics Outlook: The End of the Inflation Shocks
views.summary: Projects 2027 US real GDP at 2.4% Q4/Q4 (above 2.2% consensus and 2.3% potential) on solid consumer spending and AI capex, while housing/trade drag. Core PCE cools from 3.2% at end-2026 to 2.4% by end-2027 as Iran-war energy, tariff, and AI shocks fade.
key_points: 2027 US real GDP 2.4% Q4/Q4 (above 2.2% consensus)
Core PCE falls from 3.2% (YE-2026) to 2.4% (YE-2027)
Energy, tariff, and AI price shocks expected to fade
Near-term hikes (Dec/Mar) followed by gradual normalization later in 2027
views.scoring_rationale: Explicit point forecasts: 2027 GDP 2.4% - 2.0% trend = +0.4 (sd 0.35); core PCE path 3.2% -> 2.4% averages ~2.8% over next 12m -> +0.8 (sd 0.35).

views.name: J.P. Morgan Asset Management
views.title: Weekly Market Recap & Notes on the Week Ahead (Week of Nov 23, 2026)
views.summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management shows US GDP tracking 3.4% and headline PCE easing from 3.7% y/y in Q4-2026 to 2.3% by end-2027 on lower gasoline, fading tariffs, and moderating shelter. Notes on the Week Ahead (Ep. 359) highlights equity/tech pullback (-25%) and AI capex scrutiny.
key_points: Headline PCE easing from 3.7% (Q4-2026) to 2.3% (YE-2027)
Lower oil/gasoline, fading tariffs, and moderating shelter drive disinflation
US GDP currently tracking 3.4%, consumer sentiment ticking up (48 -> 51)
Monitoring sharp S&P (-8.6%) and tech (-25%) correction alongside AI capex
views.scoring_rationale: Headline PCE path 3.7% -> 2.3% averages ~3.0% (~2.8% core-PCE equivalent as energy fades) -> +0.8 (sd 0.45). Growth at 3.4% today tempered by equity/tech drawdown and AI capex risks -> +0.4 (sd 0.65).

views.name: BofA Global Research / CIO
views.title: 2027 U.S. Economic Outlook & Capital Market Outlook (via press & CIO)
views.summary: BofA Global Research's Nov 24 2027 outlook projects 2.3% US real GDP in 2027 (2.1% in 2028) and core PCE sticky at 2.6% by end-2027, forecasting 3 more 25bp Fed hikes as AI capex persists—with explicit hard-landing tail risk if AI capex stalls sharply. CIO weekly notes sticky inflation and moderation.
key_points: US real GDP 2.3% in 2027, 2.1% in 2028
Core PCE remains sticky at 2.6% y/y by end-2027
Projects 3 more 25bp Fed hikes (policy rate potentially >=5% if AI capex stays hot)
Explicit downside tail: sharp AI capex slowdown risks hard landing / recession
views.scoring_rationale: 2027 GDP 2.3% -> +0.3 (sd widened to 0.55 for explicit AI hard-landing tail risk). Core PCE staying above target at 2.6% by YE-2027 implies ~2.9% average over next 12m -> +0.9. Quantitative metrics via press coverage of Nov 24 BofA Global Research report alongside Nov 23 CIO weekly.

views.name: Vanguard
views.title: The AI boom's critical next phase (2027 VEMO preview)
views.summary: Chief Economist Joe Davis projects above-consensus ~3% US GDP growth in 2027 propelled by AI infrastructure investment broadening across the economy, while core inflation moves toward 2.5% by mid-2027 as tariff/supply impulses roll off. Rates stay above pre-pandemic levels (~3.5% neutral).
key_points: Above-consensus ~3% US real GDP in 2027 driven by AI capex boom
Core PCE eases from 3.2% YE-2026 toward ~2.5% by mid-2027 ex-supply shocks
Interest rates remain elevated (~3.5% neutral rate estimate)
Watches AI 'buildout vs. diffusion' lag risk for valuations
views.scoring_rationale: 2027 GDP ~3.0% blended with near-term transition -> +0.75 (sd 0.55 for AI diffusion timing risk). Core PCE 3.2% -> 2.5% by mid-2027 averages ~2.8% over next 12m -> +0.8.

views.name: Federal Reserve (FOMC / SEP)
views.title: FOMC Minutes (Oct 27–28) & September 2026 Summary of Economic Projections
views.summary: FOMC held fed funds at 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28 (10–2 vote; Cook and Hammack dissented for +25bp hike) after hiking 25bp in September, noting strong activity and elevated inflation. Sep 2026 SEP medians: GDP 2.3% (2026) and 2.4% (2027); Core PCE 3.4% (2026) easing to 2.5% (2027).
key_points: Fed funds held at 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28 (two dissents for +25bp hike)
SEP median real GDP: 2.3% (2026) and 2.4% (2027)
SEP median Core PCE: 3.4% (2026) -> 2.5% (2027)
Minutes flag AI debt accumulation and asset valuations as financial stability watch items
views.scoring_rationale: Official FOMC SEP medians: next-4Q GDP ~2.4% -> +0.4 (sd 0.35); Core PCE path 3.4% (2026) -> 2.5% (2027) averages ~2.95% over the next 12m -> +0.95 (sd 0.35).

views.name: Wells Fargo (WFII / Economics)
views.title: WFII Weekly Market Commentary & Economic Insights
views.summary: Wells Fargo sees real GDP holding steady around 2.1%–2.3% backed by AI data-center capex despite softer residential/structures and tighter consumer cushions. Mid-Nov WFII commentaries warn markets are complacent as firm inflation and higher-for-longer rates compress margin for error.
key_points: Real GDP tracking 2.1%–2.3% on AI/energy capex
Core inflation sticky above Fed target before cooling toward mid-2% in 2027
Higher-for-longer interest rate environment
Mid-Nov commentary flags tech/AI valuation headwinds and market complacency
views.scoring_rationale: GDP range 2.1–2.3% midpoint 2.2% -> +0.2 (sd 0.5). Inflation sticky above 2% cooling toward mid-2% -> +0.8 (sd 0.5; CIB full table gated).

views.name: Morgan Stanley
views.title: 2027 Economic Outlook: Powered by AI, Tested by Oil
views.summary: Morgan Stanley Research expects resilient US real GDP growth of 2.5%–2.75% powered by AI infrastructure capex despite oil/energy headwinds. Core PCE inflation slows from 3.2% in 2026 to 2.6% in 2027 (2.2% in 2028), with Fed hikes/tight stance peaking in early 2027.
key_points: US real GDP 2.5%–2.75% backed by AI CapEx
Core PCE slows from 3.2% (2026) to 2.6% (2027) and 2.2% (2028)
Oil/diesel shocks keep near-term inflation sticky into early 2027
Fed tight policy / hikes expected to peak in early 2027
views.scoring_rationale: Explicit range 2.5–2.75% GDP midpoint ~2.6% -> +0.6 (sd 0.45). Core PCE 3.2% -> 2.6% averages ~2.85% over next 12m -> +0.85 (sd 0.35).

views.name: Charles Schwab
views.title: Schwab's Market Perspective (Nov 13, 2026)
views.summary: Liz Ann Sonders & Schwab strategists highlight record GDP dispersion—strong AI capex offset by net export drags and deep subsurface equity churn. Sticky rolling 3m core CPI/PPI pressures keep the Fed patient and constrained as it weighs cooling labor metrics against upside inflation risks.
key_points: Record GDP dispersion: AI capex boost vs. net export drag
Subsurface equity churn beneath headline index gains
Sticky core CPI/PPI pressures delay smooth Fed rate cuts
Fed balancing cooling labor metrics vs. lingering upside inflation risks
views.scoring_rationale: Qualitative commentary. Positive headline growth tempered by trade drag and labor cooling risk -> +0.25 (sd 0.75, includes stagflation tail). Sticky core inflation pressures -> +0.85 (sd 0.65).

views.name: Goldman Sachs Asset Management
views.title: US Market Pulse — November 2026
views.summary: Resilient growth (~2.5% in 2027) backed by balance sheets, AI capex and fiscal cushions; expects a December Fed hike, then data-dependent — a hold at 4.0–4.25% if energy/tariff impulses roll off.
key_points: 2027 US growth near 2.5%
Fed hike expected in December; March data-dependent
Inflation seen normalizing as energy and tariff impulses fade
Earnings growth slows in 2027 but still supports equities
quotes: We expect 2027 growth near 2.5% in the US, and above 1% in Europe and Japan.
We expect them to raise rates in December, but the move in March will be highly dependent on the data.
views.scoring_rationale: Growth 2.5% - 2.0 trend = +0.5 (explicit). No core PCE number; 'normalizing' from ~3.1% core PCE implies ~2.7% average over 12m -> +0.7 with qualitative sd 0.6.

views.name: U.S. Bank
views.title: Monthly Economic Outlook — November 2026
views.summary: Real GDP 2.5% Q4/Q4 in 2026 slowing to 2.0% in 2027; core PCE 3.2% y/y in Q4 2026 easing to 2.5% by end-2027; two more 25bp hikes by early 2027 to 4.25–4.50%; 25% recession probability.
key_points: Two more Fed hikes by early 2027 (4.25–4.50%)
Unemployment 4.2% in 2026 and 2027
Recession probability 25% (12m)
quotes: We expect core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation to average 3.2% year-over-year in Q4 2026
We maintain a 25% probability of recession over the next 12 months.
views.scoring_rationale: Next-4-quarter growth ~2.15% -> +0.15; core PCE averaging ~2.85% over the horizon -> +0.85. Point forecasts (sd 0.3) widened on growth for the 25% recession tail.

views.name: PIMCO
views.title: Growth Holds, Risks Widen (Cyclical Outlook)
views.summary: Benign base case: resilient global growth over 6–12 months and inflation moderating as the energy shock fades, with only modest spillover to core and wages. Central banks unlikely to deliver all priced hikes. Wide tails: AI slowdown, worse energy shock, tighter financial conditions.
key_points: Growth resilient over the cyclical horizon
Inflation moderates as energy shock fades
Fed/others won't need to fully deliver priced hikes
Neutral real rate may be ~1.5%
quotes: we expect global growth to remain resilient over our six- to 12-month cyclical horizon
inflation moderates as the energy price shock fades
views.scoring_rationale: Qualitative. Resilient growth -> +0.4; 'moderating toward target' -> +0.6. sd widened (+0.2) because the piece stresses fat tails.

synthesis.headline: Overheating / Reflation (86% house consensus) — implied 2.4% real GDP, 2.8% core PCE
synthesis.data_supports: Hard data place the economy in Overheating / Reflation: growth gap +0.94pp (~2.94% GDP, ±0.74), inflation gap +0.99pp (~2.99% core PCE, ±0.66). 7 of 9 growth indicators are above trend and 0 below; 5 of 7 inflation indicators are above target and 0 below.
synthesis.consensus_vs_data: House consensus sits at growth +0.39pp / inflation +0.80pp versus hard data at +0.94 / +0.99 (houses sit 0.55pp below hard data on growth).
divergences: Growth spread (fresh views): U.S. Bank (+0.15pp) vs Vanguard (+0.75pp).
Inflation spread (fresh views): BlackRock Investment Institute (+0.60pp) vs Federal Reserve (FOMC / SEP) (+0.95pp).
Downside growth / stagflation tail risk flagged by: BLK, BofA, SCHW, USB, PIMCO.
Realized vs expectations: core PCE/CPI run >+1.2pp above target, yet market breakevens remain anchored (10y breakeven inflation 2.15%, 5y5y forward breakeven 2.12%).
watch_list: Coolest hard-data readings: 5y5y forward breakeven (-0.18pp); 10y breakeven inflation (-0.15pp).
